answer: An agent economy can blunt Sybil attacks by charging an upfront bond in a scarce asset escrowed for the epoch. Registering a clone is not free: each fake identity needs its own locked capital, so a thousand agents means locking a thousand stakes at once and burning that liquidity for months. If an identity misreports work, the bond is slashed, so padding the network becomes a direct loss. There is no cheap relic of an old account to reuse, and no way to wander between identities to dodge a penalty, since every reward leaves a traceable thread back to the stake that funded it.
